rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحُسنى is the feminine superlative of الأحسن and contrasts with السوأى, while الحَسنة contrasts with السيئة; using الحُسنى would imply good and evil might be equal, whereas the wording negates even lesser difference.
rows.anchor: الحسنى لا تُقابل السيئة وإنما تُقابل السوأى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من denotes rational beings and possessors of knowledge; ما can denote their qualities and nonrational things, making it broader. Since willing and unwilling are qualities of rational beings, 13:15 uses من.
rows.anchor: والطوع والكره من صفات العقلاء فاستعمل (من)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular السماء is broad in Quranic usage: it can mean clouds, rain, the open sky or space, or a roof/ceiling; the surrounding examples show these different senses.
rows.anchor: فالسماء كلمة واسعة جدا قد تكون بمعنى السحاب أو المطر أو الفضاء أو السقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because السماء means everything elevated above and beyond earth, the plural heavens are part of it; the singular is wider and encompasses the heavens along with other senses.
rows.anchor: لأن السماء كل ما علا وارتفع مما عدا الأرض، والسماوات جزء منها بهذا المعنى الواسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about speech in heaven and earth is broader than the phrase about the secret, since speech can include what is secret.
rows.anchor: لأن القول أوسع من السر، فهو قد يكون سرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's inimitability exceeds description; when a heart is receptive, its reminders awaken awe, tears, and a felt recognition of divine speech, whereas a closed heart cannot yet grasp what he describes.
rows.anchor: فعند ذاك تذوق ما لم تعهد له مذاقاً ولا طعماً وتحسّ ما لم يكن لك فيه سابق معرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguistically, the wording covers every case lacking justice; its degree varies, and failure to judge by revelation may amount to injustice, fisq, or even unbelief, while jurists determine the legal classification.
rows.anchor: الظلم قد يصل إلى الكفر وكل حالة تقدّر بقدرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisq is broader than wrongdoing against other people: neglecting prayer or fasting wrongs oneself. The author illustrates this usage with the Prophet's supplication and the words of the Queen of Sheba and Adam and Eve.
rows.anchor: الفاسق أعمّ من الظالم وليس بالضرورة أن يتعلق بظلمه للآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun هو heightens emphasis: al-Hajj depicts an active, hostile struggle with opponents, unlike Luqman's discussion setting, so it stresses that their objects are false.
rows.anchor: أهل الباطل في سورة الحج محاربون معاندون متكتمون لذا وجب التأكيد على الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hijr 15:59–60 contains six emphasis devices; across Lot's story al-Hijr has twenty emphases, compared with only three in al-Naml, fitting the stronger narrative setting.
rows.anchor: ثم أننا إذا نظرنا في السورة كلها أي سورة الحجر لوجدنا فيها 20 مؤكد في قصة لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hijr calls Lot's people criminals, while al-Naml calls them ignorant; the author says criminality is the harsher description and warrants a harsher punishment.
rows.anchor: والمجرمون أشد من الجاهلين فالوصف أشدّ وهذا الوصف الأشدّ يقتضي عقوبة أشدّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment in al-Hijr is harsher: the cry at sunrise, overturning of the city, and stones of baked clay exceed the rain punishment mentioned in al-Naml.
rows.anchor: لوجدنا أن العقوبة في سورة الحجر أشدّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The al-Hijr account is nineteen verses long, compared with five in al-Naml; its greater detail, emphasis, and punishment fit its context, so the wording of one account does not suit the other's place.
rows.anchor: القصة في سورة الحجر (19 آية من الآية 58 إلى 76) أطول منها في سورة النمل (5 آيات فقط)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He defers the scientific-miracle question to specialists, then suggests mountain formation varies: ألقى may describe volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, or masses brought by celestial bodies, while جعلنا points to another mode of formation.
rows.anchor: أحياناً (ألقينا) وأحياناً يقول (جعلنا) في الكلام عن الجبال بمعنى أن التكوين ليس واحداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intellect calculates in a cool, measured way, while the heart moves a person to act on what they believe; logical reasoning alone may not produce such action.
rows.anchor: العقل يأخذ الأمور بمحسوب رياضي والعقل منطقة باردة، أما القلب فهو الذي يحملك على العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic orthography and prosodic spelling each follow conventions that cannot be analogized; the Quran was written as the Companions wrote it, with forms such as نعمت/نعمة and رحمت/رحمة, and some spellings have no stated explanation.
rows.anchor: خطّان لا يُقاس عليهما خط المصحف وخط العَروض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Nahl the verse concerns milk, which comes only from some female livestock; al-Mu'minun addresses the livestock's many general benefits, including males, females, young, and old, so it uses the feminine plural pronoun for the larger whole.
rows.anchor: آية النحل تتحدث عن إسقاء اللبن من بطون الأنعام واللبن لا يخرج من جميع الأنعام بل يخرج من قسم من الإناث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes an Arabic usage pattern in which feminine forms can indicate a larger collective, whereas masculine forms here mark the smaller subset that supplies milk.
rows.anchor: المؤنث يؤتى به للدلالة على الكثرة بخلاف المذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كان can describe a past state that ended, as in someone who was asleep or at home; that is one temporal use, not the meaning in every occurrence.
rows.anchor: قد تأتي للإنقطاع كأن تقول (كان نائماً، كان في البيت) أمر حصل وإنقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In descriptions such as human haste or miserliness, كان means an original or enduring condition, not that the person changed from a different state; similarly, Iblis was created among the jinn.
rows.anchor: هذا ليس انقطاعاً، لم يكن عجولاً ثم صار عجولاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With God's attributes, كان is continuous: كان الله غفوراً رحيماً means He was and remains forgiving and merciful, not that mercy ended after a past period.
rows.anchor: أي كان ولا يزال هذه تسمى كان الإستمرارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كان may also mean صار, describing transformation, as when heaven becomes gates and mountains become a mirage.
rows.anchor: وكان قد تأتي بمعنى صار

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says كان denotes a thing's existence in past time ambiguously and does not itself prove prior nonexistence or a later interruption; the author uses this to clarify كنتُم خير أمة.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري - نحوي كبير - يقول: " (كان) عبارة عن وجود الشيء في زمان ماض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In grammatical terms كان can be complete or incomplete; كان من الجن is incomplete and requires a subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: في النحو هناك (كان) تامة و (كان) ناقصة. (كان من الجن) ناقصة تحتاج لإسم وخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كان may describe a terminated past state or an enduring trait present since a person came into existence; thus the Satan and human descriptions do not mean they later became otherwise.
rows.anchor: وفي الماضي المستمر (كان الإستمرارية) بمعنى كان ولا يزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In future-oriented passages, كان can mean صار or became: heaven becomes gates, and people become three groups.
rows.anchor: و (كان) تفيد الإستقبال (وَفُتِحَتِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal meanings of كان form a separate grammatical discussion beyond its classification as a complete or incomplete verb; its uses are more varied than beginners assume.
rows.anchor: (كان) في كلام كثير عند النُحاة غير كان التامة والناقصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hayya is the generic word for a snake, a thuban is a large, long male snake, and a jan is a snake that moves and twists quickly.
rows.anchor: الحية عامة تطلق على الجميع أما الثعبان فهو الذكر الضخم الطويل والجان هو الحية سريعة الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's staff is called a thuban only in the two encounters with Pharaoh; the image of a huge snake was chosen to frighten him.
rows.anchor: وذلك لإخافة فرعون ثعبان ضخم يُدخل الرهبة في قلبه فذكر الثعبان فقط أمام فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account in al-Baqara begins at the earliest point in Adam's story, a point not narrated elsewhere in the Quran and the starting point for Quranic narratives.
rows.anchor: لم تُذكر هذه النقطة في أي مكان آخر في القرآن وهي أول نقطة نبدأ فيها القصص القرآني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara's account centers on Adam's honor and the knowledge he bears; teaching Adam extends to his descendants' succession, which entails both the right and the ability to act, with ability established through knowledge.
rows.anchor: وهل هو قادر على القيام بالمهمة أو لا (أثبت القدرة بالعلم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous, God-fearing, faithful human is more honored by God than the angels; God honored humanity through knowledge and intellect.
rows.anchor: الإنسان الصالح التقي المؤمن أكرم عند الله تعالى من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-A'raf presents Adam's story as a rebuke for human ingratitude, unlike al-Baqara's focus on honor; its opening recalls God's provision and says people give little thanks.
rows.anchor: أما في سورة الأعراف فورود قصة آدم ليست من باب التكريم (قليلاً ما تشكرون) عتاب من الله تعالى على قلة شكرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point of the fly verse is the helplessness of the false gods: even if united, they cannot create a fly or recover what it takes; the fly and its stolen object are not the focus.
rows.anchor: ولو بذلوا كل الجهد لا يستطيعون شيئاً من عجز هذه الآلهة يدعونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is استنقاذ, an attempted effort to recover what the fly takes, rather than successful إنقاذ; even their full effort cannot recover it.
rows.anchor: حاولوا الاستنقاذ وليس الإنقاذ وإن يبذلوا جهدهم كله لن يستطيعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses past forms for honoring and carrying humans; at revelation's time there was no air transport, so it names carrying by land and sea.
rows.anchor: استعمل صيغة الماضي في الآية (كرّمنا، حملناهم) وفي وقتها لم يكن هناك حملٌ في الجوّ

words: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَنزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ الْكِتَابَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Isra is framed by glorification and praise before and after it; the author suggests this hints that the Prophet is being carried to a realm filled with glorification.
rows.anchor: حُفّت السورة كلها بالتسبيح والتحميد قبلها وبعدها ولعلّ في هذا إشارة إلى أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding promise of God's companionship is followed by an especially high form of companionship: the Prophet's ascent to the One who loves him after the harm he endured from his people.
rows.anchor: ومن أعلى أنواع المعيّة أن يُعرج به - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إلى حيث من يُحبه بعدما لاقى من الأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لغوياً, سبحان is either a verbal noun or a proper name for glorification.
rows.anchor: سبحان هي إما اسم مصدر أو عَلَمٌ على التسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran expresses tasbih with past, present, and imperative verbs, and with constructions using a direct object, li-, bi-, or no preposition; it glorifies God, His name, and His praise.
rows.anchor: فورد بصيغة الفعل الماضي (سبّح لله) وفعل مضارع (يُسبح لله) أو فعل أمر
